easy.def: To open your mouth wide and breathe in when you are sleepy.
examples: I yawn when I am tired.
The cat yawns and stretches.
Dad yawned at the long show.

more.def: To open your mouth wide and take a deep breath, often when tired or bored.
examples: The long car ride made everyone yawn.
He yawned and rubbed his eyes.
Seeing someone yawn can make you yawn too.
Do not yell inside.
We yell for our team.
He yelled, "Wait for me!"
The fans yelled when their team scored.
She yelled for help when she saw the smoke.
The coach had to yell over the noise of the crowd.
Yesterday we went to the park.
I lost a tooth yesterday.
Yesterday was my birthday.

more.def: The day that came just before today.
examples: Yesterday was rainy, but today the sun is out.
I finished the book I started yesterday.
Yesterday's game was called off because of rain.
A puppy is a young dog.
The young bird can not fly yet.
My sister is too young for school.

more.def: Having lived or existed for only a short time.
examples: The young tree was only as tall as my knee.
Young children need plenty of sleep.
The team is young, but it is improving fast.
These grapes are yummy.
Mom made a yummy cake.
This soup is yummy!
The bakery sells yummy cinnamon rolls.
The picnic basket was full of yummy snacks.
The kitchen smelled of something yummy.
